SearchAliases: head in ashes face in dirt
Senses.Note: Ash-covered head and dirt-covered face describes the exposed, soiled side of engagement. Yexian Guixing answers that the pure body of the teaching looks exactly so, and Yuanwu Keqin contrasts it with gazing from the high peak.

ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: Ash-covered head and dirt-covered face describes the exposed, soiled side of engagement. Yexian Guixing answers that the pure body of the teaching looks exactly so, and Yuanwu Keqin contrasts it with gazing from the high peak.
EvidenceBody: one dusty-faced posture: direct answer, descent contrast, and verse portrait retain the same soiled engagement image
Ash on the head and dirt on the face jointly form the fixed condition; either body part alone is wider.
The ten-thousand-fathom peak is the explicit contrasting position, not a synonym for dusty-faced engagement.

DraftEvidence.ZenBend: Dirt reverses purity language: the clean body is answered with a face in the dust, and descending to meet people is set against lofty withdrawal.
DraftEvidence.CounterexampleOrLimit: The phrase can be picturesque in verse, but the retained cases use it as answer and technical contrast rather than mere appearance.
